sentences.text: By this petition preferred under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, the petitioner has challenged the notice dated 14.02.2025 (Annexure P-1) Issued by police station In-Charge, MIG colony, Indore to the petitioner requiring certain information and documents in respect of Crime No. 49/2018, registered under Sections 420, 467, 468, 34 of the IPC against the accused.
2. From the notice, it is observed that on basis of complaint of one Jitendra Soni, case has been registered against Jagdish.
In respect of the transactions certain informations have been sought for from the petitioner and also certain documents have been directed to be produced.
It has been stated that earlier similar notice was issued to the petitioner, but the same has remained without response.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:29859 2 WP-16650-2025 has absolutely no objection and is ready and willing to furnish the information and the documents to the police station.
However, the grievance is that there is a threat in the notice that the petitioner shall be arrayed as an accused in the criminal case.
4. The aforesaid apprehension in my opinion is totally misconceived.

There is no threat M/S Bajaj Finance Limited Through Smt. ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25592352/
1 independently or separately as regards arraying of the petitioner as an accused in the case.

entities.text: Bajaj Finance Limited Through Smt. ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has only been stated in the notice that if the documents and information are not submitted by the petitioner, then it shall be arrayed as an accused under Section 238 of the BNS meaning thereby that if the documents and information are furnished by the petitioner then it shall not be so arrayed.

Since, the petitioner is willing to supply the documents and information to the police station, there is no reason for it to have any apprehension of being made as an accused.
5.
In the available facts of the case, it is directed that the petitioner should comply with the notice dated 14.02.2024 (Annexure P-1) without any apprehension as raised by it in this petition.

6. With the observations as aforesaid, the petition stands disposed of.
(PRANAY VERMA) JUDGE VD M/S Bajaj Finance Limited Through Smt. ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25592352/
